reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker or PD data reported to confirm CD40 engagement by sotigalimab. Cannot assess whether the drug reached and modulated its intended target. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or immune activation markers reported to confirm downstream immune costimulation pathway engagement. Cannot assess biological activity. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint (ORR) clearly failed across all three cohorts with very low response rates: Cohort 1: 9.09%, Cohort 2: 7.69%, Cohort 3: 0%. PFS also failed across all cohorts with short durations (1.87-3.48 months). No clinical benefit demonstrated. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. All cohorts in this heavily pre-treated melanoma population (prior anti-CTLA4, anti-PD1, anti-PDL1, interferon, targeted therapy) showed poor responses. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm Phase 2 design with no control group. However, the ORR results are well below historical benchmarks for melanoma (typically 15-25% for active agents). The investigator noted termination was a 'business decision (not due to safety reason)' suggesting commercial rather than safety concerns. Multiple serious AEs reported but appear manageable. Without target engagement or pathway data, cannot determine where in the causal chain the failure occurred, but the clinical endpoints clearly did not improve.
